entries.name: Claude-Mem
entries.description: Persistent memory layer for Claude Code and other coding agents: lifecycle hooks capture each session's tool usage, a local worker compresses it into observations stored in SQLite + Chroma, and relevant context is injected into later sessions via MCP tools, so agents stop starting every session cold. Apache-2.0. Local by default under Claude Code; a hosted CMEM Pro tier exists and some other hosts default to it — keep it local.
entries.install_method: In Claude Code: /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem, then /plugin install claude-mem and restart. Or: npx claude-mem install.
entries.verification: Upstream is the creator's own repo (Alex Newman, @thedotmack); ~112K GitHub stars checked 2026-11-04, far above Kushal's 1,000-star baseline. Listed as #55 (Memory & Tokens) in the source guide.

entries.name: Cutaway
entries.description: A Claude Code skill by Nyxera0x that turns one product/creature picture into an interactive three.js 3D product page that takes itself apart: every shell, gear and part written as code (no 3D model import), a page with a button per part, exploded view with labels, checked against the reference picture in graded rounds, then filmed at 60 fps with a synced procedural score/SFX. Ships SKILL.md plus docs/JOB_DESCRIPTION.md (a persistent job file Claude reads before every build; user corrections are written into it), docs/CHECKLIST.md (a 10-12 line per-picture checklist Claude grades yes/partial/no every round), docs/LESSONS.md (the mistake log: every mistake becomes one new rule), docs/PROMPTS.md, three complete examples (tarantula, piranha, wasp) and an SFX/score kit. MIT. Built on whaleyxbt/claude-motion (MIT).
entries.install_method: npx skills add Nyxera0x/cutaway -g -a claude-code ; then once, in the installed folder: npm install && npx playwright install chromium. Needs Node.js 20+; ffmpeg for the video renders and Python 3 for the score. Use: give Claude Code a picture and ask in plain words to build it as a 3D object you can take apart; it stops at the round-2 still for your approval before filming.

entries.name: Agentation
entries.description: Agent-agnostic visual feedback tool by Benji Taylor for AI coding agents. A React component (<Agentation />) mounts a toolbar in your dev build; click any element (or select text, Cmd/Ctrl-click multi-select, or drag-select), add a note, and get structured markdown back with CSS selectors, element positions, computed styles, source-file paths and the React component tree, so the agent can grep for the exact code instead of guessing from a screenshot. Animation pause freezes CSS/JS/video mid-transition so transient states can be annotated. Two modes: copy the markdown locally, or sync annotations to the agentation-mcp MCP server so the agent reads pending annotations directly (agentation_get_all_pending / watch). React 18+ recommended (16.8+ works), dev/localhost only, desktop browsers. PolyForm Shield 1.0.0.
entries.install_method: Skill route: npx skills add benjitaylor/agentation -g. In a project: npm install agentation -D and mount <Agentation /> next to the app root (dev only). MCP route: configure the coding agent to run npx -y agentation-mcp server and pass its HTTP endpoint to <Agentation endpoint=... />; the agent then reads annotations itself instead of copy-paste. Docs: agentation.com.
entries.verification: Identity resolved from multiple independent sources, not the reel alone: the reel's caption names Agentation and its audio track is titled 'GitHub repo'; a curated design-engineering resource (checked against the live repo, Sep 2026), the deploychan MCP directory and third-party skill wrappers all resolve Agentation to benjitaylor/agentation, original work (c) Benji Taylor. 5,413 GitHub stars checked 2026-11-15 via the GitHub API - above Kushal's 1,000-star baseline, no exemption needed. entries.name: Career-Ops
entries.description: Open-source local AI job-search agent by Santiago Fernandez de Valderrama (@santifer), 800+ contributors. Scans 180+ pre-configured company portals, scores each posting 1-5 against your CV before you apply, checks posting liveness, tailors an ATS-friendly resume and cover letter per job, finds the hiring manager/recruiter and drafts outreach, plus interview prep suite and an application tracker. entries.name: TokenEconomizer (Microsoft)
entries.description: Microsoft Research plugin for Claude Code (also Codex, Copilot CLI, Pi) that cuts coding-agent cost in repositories you work in repeatedly, without changing the agent. Three mechanisms learned across a repo's sessions: micro-skills (repo facts confirmed by repeated sessions, stated at session start), tool pruning (tools that go unused are left out of later sessions via the agent's own settings), and a failure-loop guard (a judge model redirects a stuck turn, never stops it). Measured on SWE-Bench: 18.4-30.9% lower mean cost across five agent-model combinations. Everything it learns stays on your machine in ~/.tokeneconomizer; its model calls run through your own agent login. MIT.
entries.install_method: Claude Code route (clone must stay in place - the plugin runs from the clone): git clone https://github.com/microsoft/TokenEconomizer.git, then claude plugin marketplace add "$PWD/TokenEconomizer", then claude plugin install tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer. Start claude, trust the folder, run /tokeneconomizer:status; once per machine (and after Claude Code updates) run /tokeneconomizer:toolprune refresh-catalog. Requires Python 3.10+ on PATH; no API key of its own, any plan or login works.
entries.verification: Install route confirmed verbatim against the live repo README Quick start on 2026-11-18: git clone, 'claude plugin marketplace add "$PWD/TokenEconomizer"', 'claude plugin install tokeneconomizer@tokeneconomizer'; the repo root carries a .claude-plugin directory and a plugin/ folder. 7,678 GitHub stars and MIT license read from the repo page 2026-11-18; created 2026-10-13, pushed the same day (GitHub skills lane) - above Kushal's 1,000-star baseline. entries.name: terminal-phone
entries.description: An interactive iPhone inside the terminal, shared with AI agents. terminal-phone embeds an iOS Simulator, or a paired real iPhone, inline in the terminal (Ghostty, kitty, iTerm2, WezTerm, Warp, VS Code) or in a native split beside the shell: the user clicks, types, drags and scrolls, and coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) drive the same phone through a JSON CLI or an MCP server with observe / act / wait primitives, accessibility element references that reject stale screens, postcondition checks, and receipts that never replay uncertain input - so an agent can build an app, install it, tap through it, verify the result, and capture App Store screenshots and preview videos at Apple's accepted sizes. Real iPhones connect via WebDriverAgent over USB or Wi-Fi and stay view-only until the owner allows control; the passcode is never bypassed. MIT.
entries.install_method: Claude Code plugin route: /plugin marketplace add govijr/terminal-phone, then install the terminal-phone plugin (MCP tools plus a skill that teaches the agent to observe, act and verify). MCP-only route: terminal-phone mcp install (or --claude / --cursor / --codex; --print shows the entries). Standalone: the repo's install.sh curl one-liner or git clone and build (see upstream README). Requires an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 15 or later and Xcode 26 or later installed and opened once.
